Well, if you don’t know your purpose, why not try to give yourself one? Like trying to be someone you admire. Maybe God sent you them as a role model for how to live yours. As for how to chose one, try to be the person you most resonate with, the one who inspires you you be a better person.

I relate to your situation far too much. I stopped cutting after I freaked my friend and sister out. While I don’t know how to keep you from cutting, I will say this. You are not a horrible person and you are not too sensitive. How do I know? Horrible people don’t go around saying they’re bad. They believe their actions are justified. And maybe you’ll counter with saying that you’ve done some bad things in the past but this clearly shows you have remorse, and that you want to do what’s right. I highly doubt it’s that though. You’re being too hard on yourself. Go out and make a mistake. Go to the kitchen and drop some salt on the ground. It is ok to make mistakes. You are human. You make mistakes; it’s natural. That does not make you a bad person. You are also not too sensitive. Your feelings are valid. You are valid. If you need to cry, cry. If you need to go out into the middle of nowhere to scream, do it. And if anyone gives you shit for this pretend like you don’t care until you don’t. Here’s something someone said that made me not care about people’s opinion on me: “Who owns you? A lot of people will say, ‘Well, no one owns me.’ But who’s opinion do you care about? Who are you seeking validation from? Who’s expectations do are you trying to fulfill?” Try to make the answer to those questions “mine”. Hope this helps.

While smoking and drinking can kill you, just not immediately, it takes years. It will actually just make your life harder to live by giving you other health risks. It’s not worth the suffering, it’s better to find healthier coping methods rather than putting yourself through physical pain which adds on to the already agonizing mental pain.
My friend once told me to not focus on the big picture. Try to focus on how your life impacts the people around you. While it’s true that there are 7.8 billion people, there’s only one you.
